newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shanghai airport to be joint-stock venture.
newsitem.headline: China's Shanghai airport to be joint-stock venture.

text.p: Shanghai's Hongqiao Airport, one of China's three largest, is to introduce a joint-stock system by selling equity to state enterprise to raise funds, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
The airport will set up the Hongqiao International Airport Joint-Stock Co Ltd this month and shareholders will mainly be large and medium-sized state-owned enterprises, it said.

The majority of funds raised will be used to purchase part of the management rights of the new airport being built to serve Shanghai's Pudong New Area that is now being developed as China's future financial hub, it said.
A small amount will be kept to develop the Hongqiao airport.

Pudong International Airport will go into operation by end-1999 and the Shanghai Airport Joint-Stock (Group) Co, which is to be formed soon, will be entitled by the Shanghai municipal government to manage state-owned assets of the two airports, Xinhua said.
Hongqiao Airport handled 12.3 million passengers last year, an 11.5 percent rise from 1995 and far exceeding its designed capacity for 9.6 million passengers, it said.
